**Refined prompt:** Enumerate which HTTP endpoints in this NestJS RealWorld API are reachable without authentication, answering from the code (not the Swagger annotations), with each claim cited to `file:line`, and flag anything unguarded that shouldn't be.

I read every controller and all four `configure()` blocks, so this list is the complete route inventory, not a sample.

## Public — no token required

| Endpoint | Declared at |
|---|---|
| `GET /api` (`Hello World!`) | `src/app.controller.ts:5` |
| `POST /api/users` (register) | `src/user/user.controller.ts:32` |
| `POST /api/users/login` | `src/user/user.controller.ts:43` |
| **`DELETE /api/users/:slug`** | `src/user/user.controller.ts:37` |
| `GET /api/articles` | `src/article/article.controller.ts:24` |
| `GET /api/articles/:slug` | `src/article/article.controller.ts:38` |
| `GET /api/articles/:slug/comments` | `src/article/article.controller.ts:43` |
| `GET /api/profiles/:username` | `src/profile/profile.controller.ts:18` |
| `GET /api/tags` | `src/tag/tag.controller.ts:17` |

Global prefix `api` is set at `src/main.ts:8`.

## Guarded (401 without a token)

Only what's listed in a `configure()` block — `AuthMiddleware` is applied per route, never globally:
- `src/user/user.module.ts:20` — `GET /user`, `PUT /user`
- `src/article/article.module.ts:24-31` — `feed`, `POST /articles`, `PUT`/`DELETE /articles/:slug`, comment create/delete, favorite/unfavorite
- `src/profile/profile.module.ts:22` — `profiles/:username/follow`, `RequestMethod.ALL`

`TagModule.configure()` is an empty body (`src/tag/tag.module.ts:17-18`), which is why `GET /tags` is open.

## The one that matters

**`DELETE /api/users/:slug` deletes any account, with no token at all.** It is absent from `UserModule.configure()` (`src/user/user.module.ts:20` lists only `GET`/`PUT user`), the handler takes no `@User()` param (`src/user/user.controller.ts:37-40`), and it passes the param straight to `UserService.delete(email)` → `userRepository.delete({email})` (`src/user/user.service.ts:83-85`). So `DELETE /api/users/victim@example.com` from an anonymous client removes that user. Knowing an email address is the entire authentication story.

Two smaller notes:

- **"Public" is not the same as "anonymous-only."** `GET /articles`, `GET /profiles/:username` and `GET /articles/feed`-adjacent handlers use `@User('id')`, which decodes the token itself when the middleware didn't run (`src/user/user.decorator.ts`) — so these routes personalize if a token is sent and return `undefined` for the id if not.
- **A bad token on a public route is a 500, not a 401.** `jwt.verify` at `src/user/auth.middleware.ts:17` is uncaught, and the decorator has the same shape — an expired token hitting `GET /profiles/:username` throws rather than degrading to anonymous. That's LESSONS.md #79, still unfixed.

Worth separating from your CURRENT_FOCUS.md list: the ownership-check item there covers `PUT/DELETE /articles/:slug`, which at least requires *a* login. `DELETE /users/:slug` requires nothing, so it's a strictly worse hole than the ones queued. Want me to draft the fix — middleware entry plus a caller-vs-target comparison?
